```yaml
descriptor:
  id: top-noncompliant-models
  name: Top Noncompliant Models
  description: Lists the oldest managed devices by model and summarizes noncompliance.
  version: 0.1.0
  minAppVersion: 0.1.0
  author:
    name: Community
    handle: community
  category: devices
  mode: read
skills:
  - id: load_devices
    format: graph
    label: Load managed devices
    detail: Retrieves managed devices from Microsoft Graph.
    settings:
      method: GET
      path: /deviceManagement/managedDevices
      select:
        - id
        - deviceName
        - model
        - complianceState
        - lastSyncDateTime
      scopes:
        - DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All
  - id: count_by_compliance
    format: transform
    label: Count devices by compliance state
    detail: Counts devices per complianceState value.
    settings:
      kind: count-by-field
      source: "{{ load_devices.output }}"
      field: complianceState
      buckets:
        - compliant
        - noncompliant
        - unknown
  - id: sort_oldest
    format: transform
    label: Sort devices by last sync date
    detail: Orders devices by lastSyncDateTime ascending and takes the first 10.
    settings:
      kind: sort-by
      source: "{{ load_devices.output }}"
      field: lastSyncDateTime
      direction: asc
      take: 10
  - id: summarize
    format: llm
    label: Summarize findings
    detail: Generates a short report on device compliance.
    settings:
      system: >-
        You analyze managed devices for an organization. Provide concise, factual
        summaries.
      prompt: >-
        Total devices: {{ load_devices.output | length }}. Noncompliant devices: {{ count_by_compliance.output.noncompliant }}.
        Oldest 10 devices: {{ sort_oldest.output }}. Write a short report.
      temperature: 0.2
      maxTokens: 200
definition:
  triggers:
    - id: manual
      kind: manual
  result:
    summary: "{{ summarize.output }}"
    data:
      total: "{{ load_devices.output | length }}"
      noncompliant: "{{ count_by_compliance.output.noncompliant }}"
      oldest: "{{ sort_oldest.output }}"
```

```yaml
name: Dormant Guest Accounts
description: Reviews Microsoft 365 guest users and reports those that have been inactive for a long time.
slug: dormant-guest-accounts
category: security
icon: mdi:account-off
initial:
  view: summary
  data:
    daysSinceLastSignIn: 90
steps:
  - id: load-guest-users
    name: Load guest users
    type: microsoft.graph.listUsers
    settings:
      filter: userType eq 'Guest'
      select: id,displayName,userPrincipalName,createdDateTime,lastSignInDateTime
  - id: filter-dormant
    name: Identify dormant guests
    type: llm
    settings:
      system: >-
        You analyze Microsoft 365 guest user data. Return a JSON array of objects
        with id, displayName, userPrincipalName, and lastSignInDateTime for users
        whose lastSignInDateTime is older than the threshold provided in the
        prompt. If lastSignInDateTime is missing, consider the user dormant.
      prompt: >-
        Data: {{ load-guest-users.result }}\nThreshold: {{ daysSinceLastSignIn }} days ago.\nAnswer in JSON.
      model: gpt-4o-mini
  - id: summarize
    name: Summarize findings
    type: llm
    settings:
      system: >-
        You receive a list of dormant Microsoft 365 guest users. Provide a short
        report: total count, earliest lastSignInDateTime, and a comma-separated list
        of userPrincipalNames. Use only the data given.
      prompt: >-
        Dormant guests: {{ filter-dormant.result }}\nAnswer in JSON with keys
        total, earliestLastSignIn, userPrincipalNames.
      model: gpt-4o-mini
  - id: summary
    name: Summary
    type: ui.alert
    settings:
      title: Dormant Guest Accounts Report
      message: >-
        {{ summarize.result.total }} dormant guest users found. Earliest last sign-in:
        {{ summarize.result.earliestLastSignIn }}. Users: {{ summarize.result.userPrincipalNames }}.
      severity: info
```
